workEn: Popol Vuh (The Council Book of the K'iche' Maya)
title: Xe oc chi cut pa Teuh Ha
titleEn: Popol Vuh — The Houses of Cold, Jaguars, Fire and Bats; the head of Hunahpu
part: The Houses of Cold, Jaguars, Fire and Bats; the head of Hunahpu
source: Popol Vuh, “The Houses of Cold, Jaguars, Fire and Bats; the head of Hunahpu”, from the only surviving copy: the K'iche' text in the hand of Fray Francisco Ximénez, written at Chichicastenango c. 1701–1703 (Newberry Library, Chicago, Ayer MS 1515, fols. 26v–28v, left-hand column), read from the Library of Congress / World Digital Library images; public domain. The text is the manuscript's own spelling, including the colonial letters ꜩ (tz), ꜯ (tz'), ꜭ (k'), ꜭh (ch') and ꜫ (q'), v for u and w, z for s, h for j, and c/qu for both k and q. Where Ximénez's cursive makes these letters hard to tell apart, the reading of Brasseur de Bourbourg's edition (Paris, 1861), made from the same manuscript, was used as a check. Word division, punctuation, capitals and quotation marks are editorial. The ꜩ→tz button shows every word in the modern K'iche' alphabet; there an ejective or glottal stop the scribe left unmarked is supplied where the word is certain, and a word whose modern form is uncertain is simply respelled. Pronunciation: modern K'iche' values for the modern spelling, an admitted convention. No prepared audio yet. All translations were made fresh from the K'iche' for Lectorium.

sentences.t: Xe oc chi cut pa Teuh Ha.
sentences.l: They-entered again then into Cold House.
sentences.i: Then they went in again, into the Cold House.
sentences.n: xe oc 'they entered': x- completive + e 'they' + oc 'enter'. chi is chic 'again, next' with its c lost before cut, as in 019 (toggle chik). Teuh Ha: teu 'cold' (toggle tew), here written teuh, + ha 'house'. Brasseur's note: 'Teu ou teuh, le froid et aussi le vent du Nord, la bise'. The name is a description, so it is translated, like the Dark House and the Jaguar House (toggle Tewj Ja, the letters respelled). 011 named the second house of trial Xuxulim Ha, 'thick with cold inside'; this is probably the same house under a plainer name, but the text does not say so.

sentences.t: Maui ahilan teu; ꜩaꜩ chi zacbocom chupan ha, v ochoch teu.
sentences.l: Not counted the-cold; thick with zacbocom(?) inside the-house, its-home of-the-cold.
sentences.i: The cold was beyond all measure: the house was thick with hail (?) inside, the very home of the cold.
sentences.n: Maui ahilan teu 'not counted (is) the cold', that is, there was no measuring it: ahilan 'counted' (inferred, as in earlier parts; modern ajilaj 'count'). ꜩaꜩ chi 'thick with', as in 011's ꜩaꜩ chi teu vpam. zacbocom is not otherwise known: zac 'white' + bocom (not known). 'Hail' or 'ice' follows Brasseur, 'cette maison était remplie de glace' (a guess; toggle saqb'okom, only zac restored as saq). chupan is written with n, as often; the toggle gives chupam. v ochoch teu 'its home, of the cold': ochoch 'home' (rochoch below).

sentences.t: Huzu cu ꜩah teu rumal cuꜩ mamai na; xzach ri teu cumal ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: Suddenly then dried-up(?) the-cold by cuꜩ(?) mamai(?) (na); it-was-lost the cold by-them the-boys.
sentences.i: But at once the cold abated (?), through the pine cones (?); the boys brought the cold to nothing.
sentences.n: A doubtful line. ꜩah is a doubtful reading (a z-like stroke stands before the ligature); it is taken as 'dry up, cease', after Brasseur's 'le froid cessa promptement' (a guess; toggle by the letters). cuꜩ mamai na is not understood. Brasseur reads cutz mamai na and renders 'avec les glands de pin (qu'ils allumèrent)', 'with pine cones (which they lit)', and the English follows him, marked (?). The division mamai na is also doubtful: the manuscript has mama at the end of one line and ina at the start of the next, and the text follows Brasseur's division. xzach ri teu 'the cold was lost': zach 'lose, come to nothing', as in earlier parts (xoh zach 'we were lost'); x- with no doer named. cumal ꜭaholab 'by the boys': c- 'their' + umal, with the boys named after it.

sentences.t: Maui xe camic; xavi e ꜭazlic ta xzaquiric. Are ta cu xcah Xibalba chiri ta xe cam vi; maui quehe, xavi quꜩ qui vach ta xzaquiric.
sentences.l: Not they-died; just they alive when it-dawned. This (ta) then they-wanted Xibalba: there (ta) they-should-die there. Not thus; just well(?) their-faces when it-dawned.
sentences.i: They did not die; they were alive when the day dawned. What Xibalba wanted was that they should die in there; but it was not so, and they were well when the day dawned.
sentences.n: Two sentences, each closed by ta xzaquiric 'when it dawned', the refrain of this part's trials. e ꜭazlic 'they (are) alive': e 'they' + ꜭazlic 'alive'. xcah 'they wanted': x- + c- (qui- 'they' before a vowel) + ah 'want', as in earlier parts (toggle xkaj, not the xqaj 'it went down' of 019). ta … vi: the wish and its place, 'that they should die there'. maui quehe 'not so', the narrator's turn, as in 019. quꜩ qui vach is written so, with qu + the ligature; Brasseur prints c'utz, which would be ca vꜩ 'well' (the ongoing ca + vꜩ 'good'). vꜩ qui vach 'good their faces' is a way of saying 'they were well': Brasseur's note on the same phrase in ¶3, 'phrase pour dire qu'on se porte bien'. The toggle respells quꜩ by the letters (kutz).

sentences.t: Xe quel chi vloc, tacol que xe be chic e chahal.
sentences.l: They-came-out(?) again hither; summoners of-them they-went again, the guardians.
sentences.i: They came out again (?), when the guardians went once more to summon them.
sentences.n: xe quel is a doubtful reading. Brasseur reads x-e qu'el, which suggests el 'go out' (xe el vloc 'they came out', ¶2), and the English follows him: 'they came out' (inferred). An earlier part took quel as 'hang'; that does not fit here, and the toggle respells the letters. chi is chic 'again' (toggle chik). tacol que, also doubtful: tacol 'summoner, one who sends for' (taq 'send' + -ol, as in earlier parts), que 'of them' (as in banol que 'maker of them'). xe be chic e chahal 'the guardians went again': chahal 'guardian' (chah 'guard' + -al), the watchers of the houses of trial. Brasseur has 'leurs gardiens étant venus les chercher'.

sentences.t: “Naquipa la maui mi xe camic?” xꜭha chi rahaual Xibalba. Xqui maihah chic qui banoh ꜭaholab Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.l: “What la not now they-died?” said again the-lords Xibalba. They-marvelled again (at) their-deeds the-boys Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.i: “How is it that they are not dead?” said the lords of Xibalba once more. And again they marvelled at the deeds of the boys, Hunahpu and Xbalanque.
sentences.n: Naquipa 'what', here 'how is it that'. la is the unexplained particle of earlier parts (perhaps the respectful 'you', perhaps only emphasis; uncertain). mi xe camic 'they have died (just now)': mi marks a thing just done, as Brasseur notes (¶2). xꜭha chi rahaual Xibalba 'said again the lords of Xibalba': the verb is singular, as often with a group (xꜭha, not xeꜭha); chi is chic 'again'. rahaual 'its lords': r- 'its' + ahau 'lord' + -al. Xqui maihah 'they marvelled at' (inferred, as in earlier parts). qui banoh 'their deeds': banoh 'doing, deed' (ban 'do' + -oh).

sentences.t: Cate xe oc chi cut pa Balami Ha; ꜩaꜩ chi balam, balam rochoch.
sentences.l: Then they-entered again then into Jaguar House; thick with jaguars, jaguars its-home.
sentences.i: Then they went in again, into the Jaguar House: it was crowded with jaguars, a home of jaguars.
sentences.n: Balami Ha 'Jaguar House' is the third house of 011's list (balam 'jaguar' + -i + ha 'house'; toggle B'alami Ja). ꜩaꜩ chi balam 'thick with jaguars', the frame of the Cold House above. balam rochoch 'jaguars its home': r- 'its' + ochoch 'home'. balam is written twice, once at the end of one line and once at the start of the next, where Brasseur prints it once; the text keeps both, and the second is read as the start of 'a home of jaguars'. It may be a slip at the line break.

sentences.t: “Maui coh i tio; ꜭo ivech chuxic,” xe vꜭhaxic balam.
sentences.l: “Not us you-bite; there-is yours it-shall-be,” they-were-spoken-to the-jaguars.
sentences.i: “Do not bite us; there will be something for you,” the jaguars were told.
sentences.n: Maui coh i tio 'do not bite us': coh 'us' (c- + oh), the object, then i- 'you (pl.)', the doer, + tio 'bite (it)' (ti 'bite' + -o), as in an earlier part. The t of tio is the looped t of this hand that looks like h (MS hio); it is read t with Brasseur. ꜭo ivech chuxic 'there is yours, it shall be': ivech 'yours (pl.)' (iv- + ech 'possession'), chuxic 'it shall be'. That is, the jaguars will have their share. Brasseur reads it otherwise: 'vous avez autre chose à faire'. xe vꜭhaxic 'they were spoken to': the passive of ꜭha(u) 'speak', with balam, the jaguars, named after it.

sentences.t: Cate cut xqui puquih bac chi qui vach chicop. Cate cut que pacaquic chi ri chuvi bac.
sentences.l: Then then they-scattered(?) bones at their-face of-the-animals. Then then they pacaquic(?) at the on-top-of the-bones.
sentences.i: Then they scattered (?) bones before the beasts, and the beasts fell (?) upon the bones.
sentences.n: Two sentences, each opening Cate cut 'then'. xqui puquih 'they scattered (?)': puquih is the verb of an earlier part, not otherwise known; 'scatter, throw down' follows Brasseur's 'ils jetèrent des os' here (inferred). chi qui vach chicop 'at the face of the animals', in front of them. que pacaquic is a doubtful reading and is not otherwise known: que, c- (ongoing) + e 'they' (the jaguars); 'fall upon' follows Brasseur's 'ils se jetèrent avec voracité sur les os' (a guess; toggle by the letters). A heavy blot covers ri c in chi ri chuvi bac; the words are read with Brasseur. chuvi 'on top of' (chi + v- + vi 'head, top').

sentences.t: “Mi ca xe vꜩinic; mi xu tih qui ꜭux; cate vi ri mi xqui ia quib. Are qui baquil ri ca xuxic,” xeꜭha ri varanel, conohel qui qui ꜭux chire.
sentences.l: “Now (ca) they-are-finished; now it-has-tested their-heart; only now indeed (ri) they-have-given themselves. This their-bones that (ca) it-became,” they-said the watchers, all-of-them sweet(?) their-heart at-it.
sentences.i: “Now they are done for; now their hearts have been put to the test (?); now at last they have given themselves up. These bones are what has become of them (?),” said the watchers, all of them glad at heart.
sentences.n: The watchers think the bones are the boys'. Three clauses with mi 'now, just now'. On mi Brasseur's note says it 'indique un passé actuel, comme d'une chose qui vient de se faire', a thing just done. ca before xe vꜩinic is not clear (perhaps the ongoing c-); it is left out of the English. vꜩinic 'be finished, done for': vꜩin (from vꜩ 'good, complete') + -ic, as in an earlier part's coh vꜩin 'we are done for' (toggle utzinik). xu tih qui ꜭux 'it has tested their hearts': tih 'try, test', the verb of tihobal 'trial'; Brasseur's note reads it 'ils ont appris leurs cœurs' (the sense is inferred). The t of tih is the looped h-like t (B. tih). xqui ia quib 'they have given themselves (up)': ia is ya 'give' written with i. Are qui baquil ri ca xuxic 'this is their bones, what has become (of them)': baquil 'bone' (bac + -il); ca xuxic is a doubtful reading, and Brasseur reads caa xuxic, 'broyés', ground as on the grindstone (caa). varanel 'watchers' (inferred, as in an earlier part: var 'sleep' + -an + -el, those who keep the night). qui qui ꜭux chire is written so; Brasseur has quiy qui qux, which suggests qui 'sweet' (modern ki') + qui ꜭux 'their heart', 'their heart sweet at it', that is, glad (inferred; the toggle respells the letters and restores nothing).

sentences.t: Maui xe camic; xavi xere vꜩ qui vach xe el vloc pa Balami Ha. “Naquipa qui chi e vinaquil? Apa qui xe pe vi?” xeꜭha ri Xibalba conohel.
sentences.l: Not they-died; just so good their-faces they-came-out hither from Jaguar House. “What (qui) of they people? Where (qui) they-came there?” they-said the Xibalba all-of-them.
sentences.i: They did not die; they came out of the Jaguar House just as well as before. “What kind of people are they? Where have they come from?” said all of Xibalba.
sentences.n: xavi xere 'just so', as before. vꜩ qui vach 'good their faces', they were well (see ¶1). xe el vloc 'they came out hither': el 'go out' + vloc 'hither'. Naquipa qui chi e vinaquil 'what (are) they, of people': vinaquil 'peopling, kind of people' (vinac 'person' + -il); qui here and in Apa qui is not clear (perhaps 'they', perhaps a particle of the question; Brasseur 'De quelle race sont ces gens-là? D'où viennent-ils?'). xe pe vi 'they came (from) there': vi points back to the place asked about.

sentences.t: Cate chic xe oc chupam ꜫaꜫ, hun ha chi ꜫaꜫ, xa vtuquel ꜫaꜫ v pam.
sentences.l: Then again they-entered inside fire, a house of fire, only alone fire its-inside.
sentences.i: Next they went into the fire, a house of fire, with nothing but fire inside it.
sentences.n: This house has no name of its own: it is hun ha chi ꜫaꜫ 'a house of fire'. chupam ꜫaꜫ 'inside fire'. ꜫaꜫ 'fire' is written with the tresillo (toggle q'aq'). vtuquel 'alone', 'nothing but', as in 011's list (vtuquel ꜩoꜩ vpam); the t is the looped t (B. utuquel). v pam 'its inside': pam 'belly, inside', written apart from v here.

sentences.t: Maui xe catic rumal, xa bolol, xa ꜩimah vi. Xavi xere vꜩ chi qui vach ta xzaquiric.
sentences.l: Not they-were-burned by-it, only bolol(?), only ꜩimah(?) there. Just so good (chi) their-faces when it-dawned.
sentences.i: They were not burned by it; it only blazed (?) and roared (?) there. They were just as well when the day dawned.
sentences.n: xe catic 'they were burned': catic is taken as the verb 'burn' (modern k'at), with plain c; Brasseur 'ils n'en furent pas embrasés' (inferred; toggle by the letters). xa bolol, xa ꜩimah vi are not otherwise known: a pair, each with xa 'only'. Brasseur takes them of the fire: 'quoiqu'il fût extrêmement fort et des plus ardents', 'though it was very strong and most fierce'. 'Blazed' and 'roared' are guesses for the pair (toggle by the letters). Xavi xere vꜩ chi qui vach 'just so, good with their faces', the refrain again, here with chi (Brasseur's note: 'également (certainement) bons avec leurs visages; phrase pour dire qu'on se porte bien').

sentences.t: Are ta cahauaxic huzuc ta que camic chupan ri, que icou vi; maui quehe, xavi ca zach qui ꜭux Xibalba rumal.
sentences.l: This (ta) it-is-wanted: quickly (ta) they-die inside that, (where) they-pass there; not thus; just (ca) lost their-heart Xibalba because-of-it.
sentences.i: What was wanted was that they should die quickly in there, where they spent the night; but it was not so, and Xibalba lost heart because of it.
sentences.n: cahauaxic 'it is wanted': c- (ongoing) + ah 'want' + -auax, a passive, + -ic, as 019's xahauax 'it was wanted' (inferred; toggle kajawaxik). huzuc 'quickly', with its c here. que camic 'they die', que icou vi 'they pass (the night) there': icou 'pass' (ik'ow). chupan ri 'inside that (house)'. maui quehe 'not so', as in ¶1. ca zach qui ꜭux 'their hearts are lost', that is, they lose heart: zach 'lose' (¶1), ꜭux 'heart'. rumal 'because of it, of them'.

sentences.t: Xe coh chic chupan Zoꜩin Ha; vtuquel zoꜩ chupam chi ha, hun ha chi Camazoꜩ, nimac chicop, queheri Chaquiꜩam qui camizabal; huzu chuꜩinic chopor chi qui vach.
sentences.l: They-were-put again inside Bat House; alone bats inside of the-house, a house of Camazotz, great animals, like Chaquitzam their killing-instrument; at-once it-is-finished chopor(?) at their-face.
sentences.i: Then they were put into the Bat House. Inside the house there was nothing but bats: it was a house of Camazotz, great beasts, whose instruments of death were like Chaquitzam (?); whatever came before them (?) was finished at once.
sentences.n: Xe coh 'they were put' (coh 'put', inferred, as in an earlier part; MS Xecoh, divided with Brasseur). Zoꜩin Ha is the Bat House, the fourth house of 011's list, there written Ꜩoꜩi Ha and here with z (Brasseur Zotzin-ha); it is called Zoꜩi Ha in ¶5. zoꜩ is the bat (Brasseur 'chauves-souris'); the toggle gives sotz', the modern word, with the tz' supplied on the plain ligature because the word is certain (011 had respelled its ꜩoꜩ by the letters). Camazoꜩ, a name, is kept: it holds zoꜩ 'bat'. Brasseur's note says it 'signifie, qui prend ou commande les chauves-souris', but what cama is here is not certain. nimac chicop 'great animals' (nimac, the plural of nim 'great'). Chaquiꜩam is kept as a name: Brasseur's note reads it 'pointe séchée', chaqui 'dry' + ꜩam 'tip, point', and thinks it a place-name; how its 'instruments of death' are like it is not said. camizabal 'killing-instrument': cam 'die' + -iza 'make' + -bal, the ending of means. chuꜩinic 'it is finished, comes to an end' (inferred). chopor chi qui vach: chopor is clearly so in the manuscript, where Brasseur prints chupan ('inside'). Its meaning is not known; 'whatever came before them' takes chi qui vach 'before their faces' and leaves chopor aside (a guess).

sentences.t: Xe ꜭohe cu chiri chupam; xa pa vvb xe var vi. Maui xe tiyic rumal ri e ꜭo pa ha; chiri cut xqui ya vi quib hun vi rumal hun chi Camazoꜩ chi cah xpe vi;
sentences.l: They-were then there inside; only in his-blowgun they-slept there. Not they-were-bitten(?) by those they there-are in the-house; there then they-gave (vi) themselves, one (vi), because-of one (chi) Camazotz from sky it-came there;
sentences.i: So they stayed there inside, and slept only inside their blowguns. They were not bitten (?) by those that were in the house; but there they gave themselves up (?), one (?) because of one Camazotz that had come from the sky,
sentences.n: xe ꜭohe 'they were (there), they stayed': ꜭohe 'be, dwell'. xa pa vvb xe var vi 'only in the blowgun they slept': var 'sleep'; vvb 'his blowgun' (toggle uub', as 018). Each boy sleeps inside his own blowgun, out of the bats' reach. xe tiyic is a doubtful reading (the ß-like ligature read ti, as in an earlier part; B. tyic); 'bitten' is taken from ti 'bite' (inferred; Brasseur 'ils ne furent pas touchés'). e ꜭo pa ha 'those who are in the house', the bats. The next clause is not clear. xqui ya vi quib 'they gave themselves (up)', ya 'give' as in ¶2; hun vi rumal hun chi Camazoꜩ 'one, because of one Camazotz' is read with Brasseur, 'ils se rendirent à cause d'un autre Camazotz qui vint du ciel' (inferred). The first hun is taken as one of the boys, Hunahpu, for what follows. chi cah xpe vi 'from the sky it came'; Brasseur's note: 'du ciel ou d'en haut'.

sentences.t: xavi vcutbal rib ta xqui bano rumal. ꜭo ca qui ꜩonoh vi qui naoh hun acab cu ri zoꜩ, que buhuhic: “Quiliꜩ, quiliꜩ,” que ꜭha, que ꜭha hun acab.
sentences.l: just its-showing itself (ta) they-did by-it. There-were (ca) their-asking (vi) their-thought one night then the bats, they buhuhic(?): “Quilitz, quilitz,” they-say, they-say one night.
sentences.i: and that was done only so that it could show itself (?). All night long the bats were taking counsel, whirring (?): “Quilitz, quilitz,” they said, they said it all night long.
sentences.n: xavi vcutbal rib 'just its showing of itself': v- 'its' + cut 'show' + -bal (the ending of means), as an earlier part's cutbal; rib 'itself'. The clause is not clear; it is read with Brasseur's 'pour se manifester' (inferred). ꜭo ca qui ꜩonoh vi qui naoh 'there they were asking their thoughts', taking counsel: ꜩonoh 'ask' (toggle tz'onoj), naoh 'thought'. ca is not clear (perhaps the ongoing c-). hun acab 'one night', a whole night: acab with plain c (toggle aq'ab', as published). que buhuhic is not otherwise known: que 'they (ongoing)'; Brasseur 'faisant un grand bruit' (a guess; perhaps a sound word; toggle by the letters). Quiliꜩ, quiliꜩ is the bats' cry, kept as written (toggle Kilitz). que ꜭha, que ꜭha 'they say, they say', doubled, then hun acab 'all night' again.

sentences.t: Xtane cu ri zcaquin; mahabi chic que zilobic ri zoꜩ; chiri ca chacal vi ri hun ꜩam vvb.
sentences.l: It-stopped then the a-little; there-is-not any-more they-stir the bats; there (ca) standing(?) there the one tip of-the-blowgun.
sentences.i: Then for a little while they stopped: the bats stirred no longer, and there they stayed perched (?) at one end of the blowgun.
sentences.n: xtane 'it stopped', ri zcaquin 'a little (while)': tane is taken as 'stop, cease', the verb of tanenic in ¶8 (inferred; Brasseur 'Elles cessèrent cependant un peu'). mahabi chic que zilobic 'they no longer stirred': zilob 'move, stir', as an earlier part's cazilobic. chacal is not otherwise known; 'perched, standing' follows Brasseur's 'elles restèrent debout' and an earlier part's chacala 'perched' (a guess; toggle by the letters). hun ꜩam vvb 'one tip of the blowgun': ꜩam 'nose, tip'. Brasseur has the bats standing 'à une extrémité de la sarbacane'; the one perched there is not named, and the English takes it as the bats.

sentences.t: Xcha cu ri Xbalanque: “Hunahpu, cahanic pa v zaquiric? Ca vilo.” “Cahanican labalo; vila na,” xꜭha cut.
sentences.l: Said then the Xbalanque: “Hunahpu, beginning(?) (pa) its-dawning? (Ca) I-see-it(?).” “Beginning(?) labalo(?); I-see-it first,” he-said then.
sentences.i: Xbalanque said: “Hunahpu, is the dawn beginning (?)? Look and see (?).” “Perhaps it is beginning (?); let me look,” he said.
sentences.n: Xcha 'he said', with plain c, as written (elsewhere xꜭha). cahanic and cahanican are not otherwise known (cahanican is also a doubtful reading); 'beginning' follows Brasseur's 'Le jour commence-t-il à poindre … Peut-être commence-t-il' (inferred; toggle by the letters). pa marks the question, as in earlier parts. v zaquiric 'its dawning'. Ca vilo is read as 'look' after Brasseur's 'regarde donc' (he reads c'av'ilo, 'you see it'); by the letters it is ca + v- 'I' + il 'see' + -o, 'I see it', as 017's ca vilo, and the English marks the doubt. labalo is not otherwise known and is a doubtful reading; 'perhaps' follows Brasseur. vila na 'let me see first': v- 'I' + il 'see' + -a, na 'first', as in an earlier part.

sentences.t: Qui cu are ca rah mucum vloc chu chi vvb, ca rah ril vloc v zaquiric; catepuch ta xcupix v holom rumal Camazoꜩ, cupul chi canoc v nimal ri Hunahpu.
sentences.l: (Qui) then this (ca) he-wants peering(?) hither at-its mouth of-blowgun, (ca) he-wants he-see hither its-dawning; then-also it-was-cut-off(?) his-head by Camazotz, cut-off(?) (chi) left-behind his-greatness the Hunahpu.
sentences.i: So it was that he wanted to peer out (?) at the mouth of the blowgun, wanting to see the dawn; and then his head was cut off by Camazotz, and the body (?) of Hunahpu was left behind without it.
sentences.n: Qui cu are 'and so it was': qui is not clear here and is left out of the English. Ximénez first wrote carah cu mucum vloc chuꜩam vvb at this point and struck it through (it anticipates these words); it is not printed. ca rah 'he wants': rah 'want', the fixed form of earlier parts; the r is written like a capital X (B. r'ah), a doubtful reading. mucum is taken as 'peering, looking out' (perhaps the muc 'look' of an earlier part; Brasseur 'regarder à la bouche de sa sarbacane'; inferred). chu chi vvb 'at the mouth of the blowgun': chi 'mouth' (toggle chi'). ril 'he sees it': r- 'he' + il 'see'. xcupix 'it was cut off': cup + passive -ix; an earlier part read 'was caught, seized', and here the sense is plain (Brasseur 'sa tête fut … coupée'). cupul 'cut off (?)', the same root (inferred). v nimal 'his greatness' is taken as his body, the bulk of him (Brasseur 'le corps de Hunahpu resta privé de la tête'; inferred). canoc 'left behind'.

sentences.t: Huchatic: “Ma mi xzaquiric?” xꜭha ri Xbalanque. Mahabi chic chi zilobic ri Hunahpu.
sentences.l: Huchatic(?): “Not now it-dawned?” he-said the Xbalanque. There-is-not any-more (chi) stirring the Hunahpu.
sentences.i: Again (?): “Has it not dawned yet?” said Xbalanque. But Hunahpu no longer stirred.
sentences.n: Huchatic is a doubtful reading (the ß-like ligature read ti; MS chaßic, B. huchatic). It is not otherwise known; 'once more' follows Brasseur's 'Puis une autre fois' (perhaps hun 'one' + a word of time; a guess). Ma mi xzaquiric 'has it not dawned (already)?': ma 'not', mi 'now, just now'. Mahabi chic chi zilobic 'there was no more stirring', as of the bats above.

sentences.t: “Hupacha ma xa on mi xbec Hunahpu? Hupacha mi xa bano?” Mahabi chic chi zilabic, xa qui chi co zoz chic.
sentences.l: “How? (Ma) only perhaps now he-went Hunahpu? How now you-did-it?” There-is-not any-more (chi) stirring; only (qui chi) there-is lying(?) now.
sentences.i: “How is it? Can it be that Hunahpu has gone? What have you done?” But there was no more stirring; he only lay there sprawled (?).
sentences.n: Two questions with Hupacha 'how'. xa on 'only perhaps' (on 'perhaps'). mi xbec Hunahpu 'has Hunahpu gone (just now)?': xbec 'he went'; the b is clear in the manuscript, where Brasseur prints x-pec. mi xa bano 'what have you done?': xa 'you (did)', bano 'do'. zilabic is a doubtful reading (the o of zilobic written as a, or a variant); taken as the same word, 'stirring'. xa qui chi co zoz chic is not understood. co is taken as ꜭo 'there is' written with plain c (as in an earlier part), and zoz is a doubtful reading (the final z has a tail and may be ꜩ). 'Lay there sprawled' follows Brasseur's 'restant là seulement étendu (comme un mort)' (a guess; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: Catecut xu quixbih Xbalanque: “Acaroc! mi xca yayan,” xcha cut.
sentences.l: Then it-shamed(?) Xbalanque: “Alas! now we yayan(?),” he-said then.
sentences.i: Then Xbalanque was filled with shame (?): “Alas! We are undone (?),” he said.
sentences.n: xu quixbih 'it shamed (him) (?)': not otherwise known; Brasseur 'se sentit rempli de honte et de tristesse' (inferred; perhaps beside the quixbic 'fear' of an earlier part; toggle by the letters). Acaroc is a cry of grief, 'alas' (Brasseur 'Hélas!'; toggle Akarok). mi xca yayan: xca 'we (did it)'; yayan is not otherwise known; 'we are undone' follows Brasseur's 'nous sommes assez vaincus' (a guess). xcha 'he said', with plain c.

sentences.t: Chila cut xbe colana vi v holom chuvi hom, xavi vꜩih Huncame, Vvcub Came. Que quicot cu ri Xibalba conohel rumal v holom Hunahpu.
sentences.l: There then it-went to-be-set(?) there his-head on-top-of the-ball-court, just its-word Huncame, Vucub Came. They-rejoice then the Xibalba all-of-them because-of his-head Hunahpu.
sentences.i: Then his head was taken and set (?) over the ball court, by the word of Huncame and Vucub Came. And all Xibalba rejoiced over Hunahpu's head.
sentences.n: xbe colana vi 'it went to be set there': colana is not otherwise known; it is taken as 'set, hang', after Brasseur's 'On alla ensuite placer la tête' and colan 'hanging' in ¶8 (inferred; toggle by the letters). chuvi hom 'on top of the ball court': hom 'ball court'. xavi vꜩih 'just its word', by the command of: vꜩih 'its word' (v- + ꜩih). Huncame, Vvcub Came 'One Death, Seven Death', the two chief lords of Xibalba. que quicot 'they rejoice', ongoing. The father's head, too, was set up by the lords' order, among the branches of the calabash tree (011); the text does not draw the parallel.

sentences.t: Cate cut ta xu tac chicop ronohel, ziz, ac, ronohel chuti chicop, nima chicop, chacab;
sentences.l: Then then (ta) he-sent-for animals all, coati(?), ac(?), all small animals, great animals, at-night;
sentences.i: Then he summoned all the animals, the coati (?) and the peccary (?), all the small animals and the great animals, in the night;
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). xu tac 'he sent (for)': taq 'send', here 'summon' (Brasseur 'Xbalanqué convoqua toutes les brutes'). The doer is Xbalanque, named in the speech that follows. ziz is the animal of an earlier part, taken there as 'coati' (Brasseur here 'Porcs-Epics', porcupines; inferred). ac is not met in this spelling before; Brasseur has 'Sangliers', wild boar, and 'peccary' rests on that and on the aꜫ 'peccary' of 015–016, listed there beside ziz as here, of which ac may be a spelling with plain c (inferred) (the toggle respells the letters; in modern K'iche' aq is the pig and ak' the fowl, and which is meant is not certain). chuti chicop, nima chicop 'small animals, great animals', a pair for all of them; the t of chuti is the looped t. chacab 'at night' (chi + acab, toggle chaq'ab').

sentences.t: xavi xare racabal ta xuꜩonoh cut quecha: “Naqui tac pa ivecha chi huhunal? Are quix nu tac vi chi cam vloc ri ivecha,” xꜭha cut Xbalanque chique. “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: just (xare) its-night (ta) he-asked then their-food: “What (tac) (pa) your-food each-one? This (is why) you I-send there: to take hither the your-food,” he-said then Xbalanque to-them. “Good bala,” they-said then.
sentences.i: and that same night he asked them about their food: “What is the food of each one of you? This is why I have sent for you: so that you may take your food,” Xbalanque said to them. “Very well,” they said.
sentences.n: xavi xare racabal 'just in its night', the same night: xare is taken as xa are 'only this' run together (as Brasseur's xavixare), racabal 'its night' (r- + acab 'night' + -al; toggle raq'ab'al). xuꜩonoh 'he asked': v- 'he' + ꜩonoh 'ask'. quecha 'their food': qu- 'their' + echa 'food' (ivecha 'your food'). Naqui tac pa is a doubtful reading: naqui pa 'what (is it)?', with tac, the plural of things many and various, between. chi huhunal 'each one' (hun doubled + -al). Are quix nu tac vi 'this is why I send for you': quix 'you (pl.)' (c- + ix) + nu- 'I' + tac 'send'. quix is a doubtful reading (B. qu'yx). chi cam vloc 'that (you) take hither': cam 'take' (toggle k'am). Vꜩ bala 'very well', the house rendering.

sentences.t: Ta xe bec e camol rech, ta xe ul he cut conohel. ꜭo xa cumar rech xbe v cama; ꜭo xa ꜩalic xbe v cama; ꜭo xa abah xbe v cama; ꜭo xa vleu xbe v cama.
sentences.l: Then they-went, they takers of-theirs, then they-arrived going(?) then all-of-them. There-are only rotten(?) of-it it-went its-taking; there-are only ꜩalic(?) it-went its-taking; there-are only stone it-went its-taking; there-are only earth it-went its-taking.
sentences.i: So they went, each to take its own, and then all of them arrived (?). Some went to take what was rotten (?); some went to take grasses (?); some went to take stones; some went to take earth.
sentences.n: e camol rech 'they (are) takers of it', each to take its own: camol 'taker' (cam 'take' + -ol), rech 'of it'. xe ul he 'they arrived, going (?)': he is the 'go' of earlier parts (inferred). Then four lines, each ꜭo xa … xbe v cama 'there are (some) only … it went its taking': ꜭo 'there is', used for 'some'; v cama 'its taking' (inferred, as in earlier parts; Brasseur 'il y en eut qui allèrent prendre'). The four foods are a litany and are kept together. cumar is taken as 'rotten, decayed', after Brasseur's 'ce qui était en putréfaction' (a guess; plain c kept where Brasseur has g; toggle by the letters). ꜩalic is not otherwise known; 'grasses' follows Brasseur's 'des herbes' (a guess). abah 'stone', vleu 'earth'.

sentences.t: Halahoh quecha ri chicop, nima chicop.
sentences.l: Different their-food the animals, great animals.
sentences.i: The food of the animals, of the great animals, was of many kinds.
sentences.n: Halahoh 'different, of many kinds' (hal 'change'). quecha 'their food', as above. ri chicop, nima chicop 'the animals, the great animals': the second half of the pair of ¶5's opening (chuti chicop, nima chicop). The passage seems to tell why each animal eats what it eats, though the text does not say so.

sentences.t: Qui pu ca v xambe canohoc ri tiz coc, xbe v cama cubulcutih; chuꜩam ca petic, are cut xoc halvachibal v holom Hunahpu;
sentences.l: (Qui) (pu) (ca) its-last left-behind(?) the tiz(?) turtle, it-went its-taking waddling(?); at-its-tip (ca) coming, this then it-entered (as) the-likeness of-his-head Hunahpu;
sentences.i: And the very last, left behind (?), was the turtle, which went waddling (?) to take its share; and as it came up to the end (of the body) (?), it became the likeness of Hunahpu's head;
sentences.n: A difficult line. Qui pu ca is not clear (Brasseur reads cu u, 'then the'); it is left out of the English. v xambe 'the last of them', as in 016 (inferred; Brasseur 'A la suite des autres'). canohoc is taken as 'left behind', beside canoc (inferred; Brasseur canah-oc). coc here is the turtle (Brasseur 'la Tortue'): the same letters as the coc 'smell' of an earlier part, a different word (toggle kok). tiz is a doubtful reading: the ligature and the z are retouched in dark ink, and the word is read with Brasseur; its meaning is not known, and Brasseur's 'enveloppée dans sa carapace' may render it, 'in its shell' (a guess). cubulcutih is also doubtful (the MS looks like cubulcahh; read with Brasseur). 'Waddling' follows his 'en faisant des zigzags' (a guess). chuꜩam 'at its tip, its end' (chi + v- + ꜩam 'tip'); Brasseur supplies '(du cadavre)', the end of the body where the head had been. halvachibal 'likeness, a changed face': hal 'change' + vach 'face' + -ibal, as an earlier part's vhalvachixic (inferred). xoc 'it entered', here 'it became'.

sentences.t: libah chi xcotix v bac v vach. ꜩaꜩ chi ahnaoh chi cah xpe vi; are v ꜭux cah, Huracan, xul coloc, xulu culoc chiri pa Zoꜩi Ha.
sentences.l: instantly (chi) it-was-carved(?) its-bone his-face. Many (chi) wise-ones from sky they-came there; this the heart of-sky, Huracan, he-came coloc(?), he-came(?) culoc(?) there in Bat House.
sentences.i: at once its eyes were carved (?). Many wise ones came from the sky: it was the Heart of Sky, Huracan, who came hovering (?), who came down (?) there into the Bat House.
sentences.n: libah chi 'instantly'. xcotix 'was carved (?)': perhaps the root of modern k'ot 'carve', with plain c (B. x-qotox, with o for i); Brasseur 'à l'instant même il s'y sculpta des yeux' (inferred; toggle by the letters). v bac v vach 'his eyes' (the house rendering of vbac vvach, 'its bone, his face'). ꜩaꜩ chi ahnaoh 'many wise ones': ahnaoh 'one who knows' (ah- + naoh 'thought'). v ꜭux cah 'Heart of Sky', written here in three words; Huracan named beside it, as in the creation. xul coloc, xulu culoc is a couplet, but a doubtful one: xulu culoc looks like xuh culoc in the manuscript and is read with Brasseur (x'ulu c'uloc). coloc and culoc are not otherwise known; Brasseur 'Hurakan même vint planer au-dessus de la maison', 'came to hover', is followed (a guess; toggle by the letters). Zoꜩi Ha, the Bat House, the Zoꜩin Ha of ¶4 (Brasseur Zotziha).

sentences.t: Ma cu atan xuꜩinic v vach; vꜩ chic xuxic;
sentences.l: Not then quickly(?) it-came-right its-face; good now it-became;
sentences.i: The face did not come right quickly (?), but it came to be good;
sentences.n: atan is not otherwise known; 'quickly' follows Brasseur's 'ne s'acheva pas si promptement' (a guess; toggle by the letters). xuꜩinic 'it came right, was finished' (from vꜩ 'good'). vꜩ chic xuxic 'good now it became': chic 'now, already'. The face is the turtle's, becoming Hunahpu's.

sentences.t: xavi xare v chuuc hebel xvachinic; xavi xare xꜭhauic.
sentences.l: just (xare) its-hair(?) fine(?) it-showed-itself; just (xare) it-spoke.
sentences.i: likewise its hair (?) showed itself fine (?); likewise it spoke.
sentences.n: xavi xare 'just so, likewise', twice, a pair (xare as above). v chuuc is a doubtful reading (n or u; B. chuuk); 'its hair' follows Brasseur's 'sa chevelure' (a guess; toggle by the letters). hebel is taken as 'fine, handsome' (perhaps the modern jeb'el 'pretty'; inferred). xvachinic 'it showed itself, took shape' (vach 'face' + -in). xꜭhauic 'it spoke'.

sentences.t: Are cut ta chi rah zaquiric, chi cactarin v xecah, ca xaquinuchic.
sentences.l: This then when (chi) it-wants dawning, (chi) reddened(?) its-foot-of-sky, (ca) xaquinuchic(?).
sentences.i: And when the day was about to dawn, and the foot of the sky was reddening (?), the opossum spread its legs (?).
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). chi rah zaquiric 'it wants to dawn', that is, the dawn was near: rah 'want', as in ¶4. cactarin is not otherwise known; it is taken as cac 'red' + -tar + -in, 'reddening', after Brasseur's 'l'aurore colorait l'horizon' (inferred; toggle by the letters). v xecah 'its foot of the sky', the horizon: xe 'foot, root' + cah 'sky', as an earlier part's vxecah 'the world under the sky'. ca xaquinuchic is one word in K'iche' of a kind not met before. Brasseur's note: xaquin means 'ouvrir les jambes', and vuch is the opossum; 'pour exprimer que le jour paraît, on dit textuellement, le sarigue entr'ouvre les jambes' (inferred; toggle by the letters). The opossum is the animal of the creator name Hunahpu Vuch, 'Hunahpu Opossum' (001).

sentences.t: “Ama xuchux ri vuch?” “Ve,” xꜭha ri mama.
sentences.l: “(Ama) it-has-done(?) the opossum?” “Yes,” he-said the old-man.
sentences.i: “Has the opossum done it (?)?” “Yes,” said the old man.
sentences.n: Ama is not otherwise known; it is taken as a particle of the question (inferred). xuchux is read with Brasseur's note, 'Ama a-u chux ri vuch, est-ce que c'est fait le sarigue?', with chux 'become, be made' (inferred; toggle by the letters). vuch 'opossum'. Ve 'yes', as in an earlier part. ri mama 'the old man': here the opossum himself. Brasseur's note: 'Au lieu du sarigue ici c'est un vieillard', and he links him with Hun-Ahpu-Vuch, the creator name.

sentences.t: Ta chi xaquinic, cate ta chi queꜫumar chic; cahmul xaquin ri mama. “Ca xaquin v vuch,” ca ꜭha vinac vacamic.
sentences.l: Then (chi) he-spread-legs(?); then (ta chi) it-grew-dark again; four-times he-spread-legs(?) the old-man. “(Ca) he-spreads-legs(?) the opossum,” (ca) they-say people now.
sentences.i: Then he spread his legs, and then it grew dark again; four times the old man spread his legs. “The opossum is spreading its legs,” people say to this day.
sentences.n: xaquinic, xaquin 'spread the legs' (inferred, from Brasseur's note above; toggle by the letters). queꜫumar 'grow dark' (queꜫum 'darkness' + -ar), as an earlier part's xꜫecumaric. cahmul 'four times' (cah 'four' + mul 'times'): the dawn comes and goes four times. Ca xaquin v vuch 'the opossum spreads (its legs)', the saying; ca ꜭha vinac vacamic 'people say now': vinac 'people', vacamic 'now, today'. Brasseur takes the saying as said 'pour donner à entendre que le soleil se lève', and his note calls it a 'proverbe qui paraît inusité aujourd'hui'.

sentences.t: Xa cu cac raxaꜩinic ta xu tiquiba v ꜭohic.
sentences.l: Only then red(?) blue-green(?) when it-began its-being.
sentences.i: It was only when the sky was red and blue-green (?) that it began to live (?).
sentences.n: The manuscript has xuhquiba, a misprint for xu tiquiba, corrected here: the t is the h-like t of this hand, with no i, as in 017's identical case (Brasseur tigiba). xu tiquiba 'it began': x- + v- 'it' + tiquiba 'plant, begin', the planting verb of the book's preamble. cac raxaꜩinic is not clear: cac is taken as 'red' (toggle kaq), raxaꜩinic as rax 'green, blue' + -aꜩinic (not otherwise known). Brasseur: 'Au moment où l'aurore couvrit l'horizon de ses brillantes couleurs' (inferred). v ꜭohic 'its being, existence' (ꜭo 'be' + -ic; Brasseur u qoheic, 'il commença à exister'). The head begins to live.

sentences.t: “Ma vꜩ cha chux cut Hunahpu he?” “Vꜩ,” xꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “(Ma) good (cha) it-shall-be then Hunahpu (he)?” “Good,” he-said then.
sentences.i: “Will it do, then, for Hunahpu (?)?” “It will do,” came the answer.
sentences.n: A doubtful line. Ma vꜩ 'is it good?' (ma marks the question). cha may be 'he said' or a particle (Brasseur 'Ma utz, cha, ch'ux cut Hunahpu he?'). chux 'it shall be' (ch- + ux 'become'). he at the end is not clear (perhaps a particle of the question). Brasseur: 'Est-elle bien ainsi, la tête de Hunahpu? demanda-t-on. — Elle est bien, répondit-on.' The English follows him; who asks and who answers is not said. The answer Vꜩ 'good' takes up vꜩ of the question.

sentences.t: Xavi xare chu baquitila v holom, quehe ri quiꜩih v holom xuxic.
sentences.l: Just (xare) he-shaped(?) his-head, thus as true his-head it-became.
sentences.i: So his head was given its shape (?), and it became like his true head.
sentences.n: baquitila is not otherwise known (the t is the looped t; B. bakitila). It is taken as 'shape, make', after Brasseur's 'l'on acheva ainsi de fabriquer sa tête' (a guess; perhaps from bac 'bone'; toggle by the letters). chu 'he (did it)', ch- + v-. quehe ri quiꜩih v holom 'like his true head': quiꜩih 'true, truly'.

sentences.t: Cate cut ta xqui ban qui ꜩih, xe pixaban quib, mana qui cut chaahic.
sentences.l: Then then (ta) they-made their-word, they-counselled themselves: not (qui) then playing.
sentences.i: Then they made their plan, and gave each other their counsel: he should not play (?).
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). xqui ban qui ꜩih 'they made their word', they agreed on what to say and do. xe pixaban quib 'they counselled one another', as in 019. mana qui cut chaahic is read with Brasseur's 'de ne pas jouer à la paume' (mana 'not'; qui not clear; cut is a doubtful reading, the MS a/u ambiguous; chaahic 'playing'). The sense is taken to be that Hunahpu, with the new head, will not play (inferred).

sentences.t: “Xa qui chayecuh avib.” “Xa in hun qui qui banouic,” xꜭha Xbalanque chire.
sentences.l: “Only (qui) you-expose(?) yourself.” “Only I one (qui) (qui) the-one-who-does,” he-said Xbalanque to-him.
sentences.i: “Only put yourself forward, then (?).” “I alone will do it all,” Xbalanque said to him.
sentences.n: Two short speeches. chayecuh is a doubtful reading and is not otherwise known: ch- + a- 'you (one)' + yecuh (perhaps the yecoub of ¶8). Brasseur renders 'Expose-toi seul alors (au danger, dirent-ils à Xbalanqué)' (a guess). avib 'yourself': a- 'your' + ib 'self'. Xa in hun 'only I, one', I alone; qui qui banouic is not clear (banouic 'do it, the one who does it', the ending that names the doer; Brasseur 'Eh bien, je ferai tout par moi-même'). chire 'to him', to Hunahpu.

sentences.t: Cate cut ta xu pixabah hun vmul: “Cat ꜭoleta chiri chuvi hom, chi vi cat ꜭohe vi chupan pixc,” xuꜭhax vmul rumal Xbalanque.
sentences.l: Then then (ta) he-charged a rabbit: “You go-be-placed(?) there on-top-of the-ball-court; (chi) there you-shall-be there inside the-pixc(?),” he-was-told the-rabbit by Xbalanque.
sentences.i: Then he gave a rabbit its orders: “Go and settle yourself (?) up there over the ball court, and stay there among the pix (?),” the rabbit was told by Xbalanque.
sentences.n: xu pixabah 'he charged, gave orders to': pixab 'counsel, command' + -ah. vmul 'rabbit'. Cat ꜭoleta 'you go and be placed (?)': cat 'you (one) shall', ꜭol 'be (put) in a place' (as ꜭolic) + -eta, an ending not met before (inferred). chi vi … vi 'there', twice. cat ꜭohe vi 'you shall be there'. pixc, and pix in ¶8 and ¶9, are not clear. Brasseur renders 'entre les glands de la corniche', 'among the acorns (ornaments) of the cornice', and in ¶8 'entre les glands (qui en ornaient la corniche)'. In modern K'iche' pix is the tomato. Which is meant is not known, and the word is kept in K'iche' in the English (toggle by the letters). xuꜭhax 'he was told': the passive of ꜭha.

sentences.t: “Chopon na quic avuꜭ, cate cat elic; ca in qui banouic,” xuꜭhax ri vmul ta xpixabaxic chacab.
sentences.l: “It-arrives (na) the-rubber with-you, then you-go-out; (ca) I (qui) the-one-who-does,” he-was-told the rabbit when he-was-charged at-night.
sentences.i: “When the ball reaches you, then come out; I will do the rest,” the rabbit was told, when it was given its orders in the night.
sentences.n: Chopon 'it arrives (there)', ch- + opon. quic 'rubber', the ball (as in 018). avuꜭ 'with you': a- 'your' + vuꜭ 'with' (toggle awuk'). cat elic 'you go out'. ca in qui banouic 'I am the one who will do it': as above, with ca, the ongoing (inferred). xpixabaxic 'he was charged': the passive of pixabah. chacab 'at night'.

sentences.t: Cate cut ta xzaquiric; xavi xare vꜩ qui vach qui cabichal.
sentences.l: Then then (ta) it-dawned; just (xare) good their-faces, the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: Then the day dawned, and both of them were well.
sentences.n: vꜩ qui vach 'good their faces', they were well, the refrain of the trials. qui cabichal 'the two of them' (inferred, as in earlier parts, after Brasseur 'l'un et l'autre').

sentences.t: Xcah chi cu qui chaah, colan chi cu v holom Hunahpu chuvi hom.
sentences.l: It-went-down again then their-game, hanging(?) still then his-head Hunahpu on-top-of the-ball-court.
sentences.i: Their game began again, with Hunahpu's head hanging (?) over the ball court.
sentences.n: Ximénez's paragraph. xcah chi cu qui chaah 'their game went down again', began again, as in 019 (cah 'go down'; chi is chic). colan 'hanging, set (?)', the colana of ¶4 (inferred; Brasseur 'au lieu où était suspendue la tête'). The real head is still over the court; the boys play with the new one.

sentences.t: “Mi xca chacoyan! Mi xi bano qui yan; mi xi yao,” xe vꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: “Now we-have-won! Now you-did their-yan(?); now you-gave(?),” they-were-told.
sentences.i: “We have won! You have suffered every shame (?); you have given in (?),” they were told.
sentences.n: Three clauses with mi 'now, just now', the lords' taunt. xca chacoyan 'we have won': chac 'win, defeat' (as in 019) + -oyan, an ending not met before (inferred). Mi xi bano qui yan, mi xi yao is not clear: xi 'you (pl.) (did)', bano 'do', yao 'give'. yan is not otherwise known. Brasseur: 'Vous avez subi toutes les hontes! Vous nous avez rendu (la palme)!' and the English follows him, marked (?). xe vꜭhaxic 'they were told'.

sentences.t: Xavi cu xere chi ziquin Hunahpu: “Chacuca ri holom chi quic,” que vꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: Just then so (chi) they-called-to Hunahpu: “Chacuca(?) the head with rubber,” they-were-told.
sentences.i: That is how they shouted at Hunahpu: “Let the head rest (?) from the ball (?),” they were told.
sentences.n: chi ziquin 'they called out, shouted (at)': ziquin 'call' (sik'in). Chacuca is a doubtful reading (B. Ch'a cuk a) and is not otherwise known. Brasseur renders 'Repose ta tête maintenant (de cette fureur que tu avais) du jeu de balle', and the English follows him (a guess). chi quic 'with, at the rubber (ball)'. que vꜭhaxic 'they are told'.

sentences.t: Ma cu chi qui ca caxou chic; chi yecoub quib.
sentences.l: Not then (chi qui ca) it-pained(?) any-more; (chi) they-held-back(?) themselves.
sentences.i: But he did not feel the hurt (?) any more; they held themselves back (?).
sentences.n: A doubtful line. The manuscript has chiqui, divided chi qui; Brasseur reads chi ca qaxou. caxou is a doubtful reading (n or u, decided with Brasseur); it is taken as the root of caxcol 'suffering' (¶10), 'feel pain' (inferred; toggle by the letters). Brasseur: 'Mais il ne souffrait pas des insultes dont on l'abreuvait'. yecoub quib: yecoub is not otherwise known (plain c kept where Brasseur has g), perhaps the yecuh of ¶7; 'held themselves back' is a guess.

sentences.t: Are cu xeꜩacou quic rahaual Xibalba; xu cul cut Xbalanque.
sentences.l: This then they-threw(?) the-rubber the-lords of-Xibalba; he-met-it then Xbalanque.
sentences.i: It was the lords of Xibalba who threw the ball (?), and Xbalanque went to meet it.
sentences.n: Are … xeꜩacou 'it is they who threw': ꜩac 'throw, strike' (inferred; Brasseur 'les rois de Xibalba lancèrent la balle élastique') + -ou, the ending that names the doers, after Are, as in an earlier part's xe chacouic. quic 'the rubber, the ball'. xu cul 'he met it': cul 'meet, receive' (modern k'ul), with plain c (Brasseur 'Xbalanqué sortit à sa rencontre'; inferred; toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: Tacal cu ri quic chuvach bate; chi tanenic ta xelic; huzu cu xicou quic chuvi hom; xa hun xa canab vi tacal pa pix.
sentences.l: Landing(?) then the rubber in-front-of the-ring(?); (chi) stopping, then it-went-out; suddenly then it-passed the-rubber over the-ball-court; only one only bound(?) (vi) landing(?) in the-pix(?).
sentences.i: The ball came down (?) in front of the ring (?) and stopped, and then it went out: at once the ball flew over the ball court, and in a single bound (?) it came down in the pix (?).
sentences.n: tacal 'landing, come to rest' (inferred, as in earlier parts). chuvach bate 'in front of the ring (?)': bate as in earlier parts (Brasseur 'anneaux'; a guess). tanenic 'stopping' (inferred; Brasseur 's'arrêta'); tane in ¶4. xelic 'it went out'. xicou 'it passed', ik'ow. xa hun xa canab vi 'in only one bound (?)': canab is a doubtful reading (B. canap), taken as 'bound, leap' after Brasseur's 'd'un seul bond' (a guess). pa pix 'in the pix': see ¶7. It lands where the rabbit is waiting.

sentences.t: Ta xel cu ri vmul chi coxcotic ta xbec; ocotal cut ta xbe cumal ri Xibalba, que huminic, que chaninic xe be chirih ri vmul; xe quiz be conohel Xibalba.
sentences.l: Then it-went-out then the rabbit hopping when it-went; chased(?) then when it-went by-them the Xibalba; they clamoured(?), they hurried(?), they-went behind the rabbit; they-finished going all-of-them Xibalba.
sentences.i: Out came the rabbit, hopping as it went, and it was chased (?) by those of Xibalba: clamouring (?), rushing (?), they went after the rabbit, until every last one of Xibalba had gone.
sentences.n: chi coxcotic 'hopping': a doubled root, a word that paints a movement, as 016's ꜩoꜩotic (Brasseur 's'en allait sautillant'; inferred). The t is the looped t (MS looks coxcohic). ocotal 'chased' is taken from ocot 'chase' (Brasseur 'poursuivi'; inferred; toggle by the letters). que huminic, que chaninic, a pair: huminic 'clamouring (?)' as in an earlier part, chaninic 'hurrying' (perhaps from chanim 'quickly'; inferred; Brasseur 'qui couraient en tumulte, vociférant derrière le Lapin'). chirih 'behind': chi + r- + ih 'back'. xe quiz be conohel 'they finished going, all of them': quiz 'finish, all'.

sentences.t: Catecut xqui camixtah ri v holom Hunahpu; xtiquixtah chic v coc Xbalanque. Are chi cut xbe qui cuba ri coc chuvi hom.
sentences.l: Then they-snatched(?) the his-head Hunahpu; it-was-planted(?) again (in) its-turtle(-place) Xbalanque. This then they-went to-set(?) the turtle on-top-of the-ball-court.
sentences.i: Then they quickly took (?) Hunahpu's head, and Xbalanque planted it again (?) in the turtle's place. Then they went and set (?) the turtle over the ball court.
sentences.n: A new paragraph (ours). camixtah, here and again below, is not otherwise known; 'snatch, take quickly' follows Brasseur's 'Xbalanqué s'empressa aussitôt de saisir la tête' (a guess; plain c kept where Brasseur has q; toggle by the letters). xtiquixtah is a doubtful reading (the h-like t with a stroke read as i; B. x-tiquix-tah); it is taken from tic 'plant' with an ending not met before, 'planted, set' (inferred). v coc 'its turtle', in the turtle's place (Brasseur 'au lieu de la tortue'; inferred). v coc Xbalanque can also be read 'Xbalanque's turtle', as v holom Hunahpu is 'Hunahpu's head'; the English takes Xbalanque as the doer, with Brasseur. The verbs are not clear about who does what: the first has 'they', the second no doer, and Xbalanque is named after it. qui cuba 'they set, placed (?)': cuba is taken as 'set down', after Brasseur's 'il alla ensuite colloquer la tortue' (inferred; toggle by the letters). chi is chic.

sentences.t: Quiꜩih holom chi cu v holom ri Hunahpu; que quicot chi cu qui cabichal.
sentences.l: True head again then his-head the Hunahpu; they-rejoice again then the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: Hunahpu's head was a true head again, and the two of them rejoiced.
sentences.n: Quiꜩih holom 'a true head': quiꜩih 'true'. chi cu is chic + cu, twice (toggle chik). que quicot 'they rejoice', as Xibalba did in ¶4: now it is the boys.

sentences.t: Are cut que be ꜩucu na quic ri Xibalba.
sentences.l: This then they-go to-look-for (na) the-rubber the Xibalba.
sentences.i: And Xibalba went off to look for the ball.
sentences.n: que be 'they go'. ꜩucu 'look for' is ꜩucuh, as in earlier parts (ka nu ꜩucuh 'I am looking for'), here without h; a doubtful reading (B. tzuku). na is not clear (perhaps 'first' or 'still').

sentences.t: Catecut xqui camixtah chiri quic pa pix, ta xe ziquin chi cut: “Quix petoc! Vae quic que mi xca rico,” xeꜭha qui colem chi cut.
sentences.l: Then they-snatched(?) there the-rubber in the-pix(?), then they-called-out again then: “You-come! This the-rubber (que) now we-found,” they-said, their-raising(?) again then.
sentences.i: Then they snatched up (?) the ball there in the pix (?), and called out: “Come! Here is the ball, we have found it,” they said, holding it up (?).
sentences.n: xqui camixtah 'they snatched up (?)', as above. pa pix: see ¶7. xe ziquin 'they called out'. Quix petoc 'come (pl.)': quix 'you (pl.)' + petoc 'come'. que is not clear here (perhaps 'thus'). mi xca rico 'we have just found it': xca 'we (did)' + rico 'find'. qui colem is not otherwise known; 'holding it up' follows Brasseur's 'en l'élevant (pour la faire voir)' (a guess; toggle by the letters). chi cut is chic + cut, here and twice above.

sentences.t: Ta xe ul Xibalba: “Naquipa ri mi xquilo?” xeꜭha cut, ta xqui tiquiba chi cut chaahic.
sentences.l: Then they-arrived Xibalba: “What the now we-saw?” they-said then, when they-began again then playing.
sentences.i: When Xibalba came back: “What was it that we saw?” they said, and they began to play again.
sentences.n: The manuscript has xquihquiba, a misprint for xqui tiquiba, corrected here: as in ¶6, the t is the h-like t of this hand, with no i, and the word runs across a line break (Brasseur x-qui tigiba). A new paragraph (ours). xe ul 'they arrived (back)'. mi xquilo 'we have just seen': here xqui- is taken as 'we' (x- + q- + il 'see' + -o; toggle xqilo), after Brasseur's 'Qu'est-ce donc que nous avons vu'. The lords cannot tell what it was they chased. xqui tiquiba 'they began' (tiquiba 'plant, begin'); chi cut is chic + cut.

sentences.t: Hunam chaahic chi cut xqui ban chic qui cabichal.
sentences.l: Equal playing again then they-did again, the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: And both sides played evenly again.
sentences.n: Hunam 'alike, equal'. chaahic 'playing'. xqui ban 'they did'. qui cabichal 'the two of them' (inferred, as above), here the two sides of the game, after Brasseur 'deux ensemble'.

sentences.t: Catecut xcacatah ri coc rumal Xbalanque, chi pucabin ri coc; xcah pa hom, zaquiram cu ri v zaquilal chi qui vach.
sentences.l: Then it-was-struck(?) the turtle by Xbalanque, (chi) shattered(?) the turtle; it-went-down into ball-court, scattered(?) then the its-whiteness at their-face.
sentences.i: Then the turtle was struck (?) by Xbalanque, and the turtle broke apart (?): it fell into the ball court, its white pieces (?) scattering before their eyes.
sentences.n: xcacatah is not otherwise known; 'was struck' follows Brasseur's 'fut atteinte d'un coup de pierre (lancée) par Xbalanqué' (a guess; toggle by the letters). pucabin is not otherwise known; 'shattered' follows Brasseur's 'tomba en pièces' (a guess). xcah 'it went down', fell (cah 'descend'). zaquiram is not otherwise known, perhaps from zac 'white'; v zaquilal 'its whiteness' (zac + -il + -al). Brasseur renders 'brisée en mille morceaux comme de la faïence aux yeux de ceux (de Xibalba)', broken into a thousand pieces like earthenware; 'white pieces scattering' is a guess. chi qui vach 'before their faces'.

sentences.t: “Naquipa ri chi be i cama? Apa ꜭo vi ri camol re?” xꜭha Xibalba.
sentences.l: “Who the shall go your(pl.)-taking? Where is there the taker of-it?” said Xibalba.
sentences.i: “Which of you will go and fetch it? Where is the one to fetch it?” said Xibalba.
sentences.n: Xibalba's cry of dismay, two questions. Naquipa ri 'what, which (one)'. chi be 'shall go' (chi before the verb). i cama 'your (pl.) taking' (inferred, the cama of ¶5). camol re 'the taker of it': camol 'taker' (cam 'take' + -ol), re 'of it'. The 'it' is presumably the head they had been playing with (Brasseur's French here is broken in the print). xꜭha is singular for Xibalba, as in ¶1.

sentences.t: Quehe cut qui chacatahic rahal Xibalba rumal Hunahpu, Xbalanque. Nima caxcol xe cohe vi; maui are xe cam vi ri ronohel xban chique.
sentences.l: Thus then their-being-brought-low the-lords(?) Xibalba by Hunahpu, Xbalanque. Great hardship they-were there; not this they-died there the all it-was-done to-them.
sentences.i: This is how the lords (?) of Xibalba were brought low by Hunahpu and Xbalanque. Great were the hardships they endured there; but they did not die of all that was done to them.
sentences.n: qui chacatahic 'their being brought low', the verbal noun, as at the end of 019. rahal is a doubtful reading: the manuscript has rahal, where Brasseur prints r'ahaual 'its lords'. A syllable may have been dropped, but this is not certain, and the English follows the sense of rahaual, marked (?) (toggle by the letters). Nima caxcol 'great hardship': caxcol, with plain c (toggle k'axk'ol). xe cohe vi 'they were (in it) there': cohe is ꜭohe 'be' written with plain c (B. qohe; toggle k'oje, as earlier parts' coheic). maui are xe cam vi 'they did not die of it': cam 'die'. ronohel xban chique 'all that was done to them'. The next part begins with the boys foreseeing their own death (Brasseur's twelfth chapter).

about: The boys go through the remaining houses of trial in Xibalba. In the Cold House the cold is past bearing, but the boys drive it off, and at dawn they are alive and well. In the Jaguar House they promise the jaguars something to eat and throw them bones; the watchers think the bones are the boys' own, but the boys come out unharmed, and Xibalba asks what kind of people they are. The Fire House does not burn them. Then they are put into the Bat House, the house of Camazotz, and sleep inside their blowguns while the bats cry "quilitz, quilitz" all night. Toward dawn Hunahpu looks out of his blowgun to see whether day has come, and Camazotz cuts off his head. Xbalanque is ashamed and grieves; the head is hung over the ball court, and Xibalba rejoices. In the night Xbalanque calls all the animals together, and each one takes its own food. Last comes the turtle, which takes the place of Hunahpu's head: a face is carved on it, many wise ones come from the sky, and Heart of Sky, Huracan, comes down into the Bat House. The dawn comes slowly; the opossum, the old man, spreads his legs four times, as people still say. The new head comes right and speaks. The boys make a plan: a rabbit is told to wait on the ball court and to bound away when the ball comes to it. In the game the lords of Xibalba mock Hunahpu, the ball flies out of the court, the rabbit runs off, and all Xibalba chases it. Meanwhile Xbalanque takes Hunahpu's real head back, puts it in place of the turtle, and sets the turtle over the court. When the game begins again Xbalanque strikes the turtle, and it falls and breaks to pieces before the lords. So Xibalba is beaten again: the boys have endured great hardships, but nothing that was done to them has killed them.
